headline: Trevi Fountain Sculptor's Lost Marble Pope Discovered in English Salvage Yard
meta_description: A rare 18th-century marble sculpture by Pietro Bracci, the artist behind Rome's Trevi Fountain, has been discovered in a Wiltshire salvage yard after centuries…
summary_short: A priceless marble sculpture by the Trevi Fountain's creator lay hidden among garden ornaments in an English salvage yard—until a sharp-eyed builder spotted it for £300.
body:
A builder's keen eye has rescued a forgotten masterpiece from obscurity. A 27-inch marble sculpture of Pope Clement XII, fashioned by Pietro Bracci as a presentation model in the 1730s, has emerged from a salvage yard in Wiltshire, England, after centuries of neglect. Bracci, one of eighteenth-century Rome's greatest sculptors and architect of the iconic Trevi Fountain, created this 'maquette' to pitch a monumental bronze commission from the Roman Senate, celebrating the pope's generous gift to the Capitoline Museums. While the original full-sized bronze was melted down for scrap metal sixty years after its completion, Bracci's marble study survived—though its remarkable origins were forgotten.

The sculpture's journey tells a story of lost legacy. Shipped to an English country estate, it gradually fell from favor, eventually exiled outdoors where it languished among hundreds of architectural castoffs. When the builder spotted it among the rubble, he recognized something extraordinary in its craftsmanship and artistic signature. Now, the Wiltshire auction house Woolley & Wallis has placed it before the world, with estimates ranging from $6,600 to $13,300.

"To have a rare eighteenth-century marble figure of Pope Clement XII by Pietro Bracci come to light is a remarkable opportunity," said furniture specialist Mark Yuan Richards. "This extraordinary survivor offers a tangible connection to the world of the papal court and the artistic splendor of the period." The discovery reminds us that treasures sometimes wait in plain sight—and that a moment of attentiveness can restore lost history to the light.
quick_facts: Sculpted by Pietro Bracci, artist behind Rome's Trevi Fountain
27-inch marble model created in the 1730s as a papal commission pitch
Purchased from Wiltshire salvage yard for £300 ($400)
Expected to auction for $6,600–$13,300 at Woolley & Wallis
Original full-sized bronze melted down 60 years after creation
